summary: Increasing work_mem and shared_buffers in PostgreSQL 9.2 unexpectedly slowed down queries, particularly those involving Hash Joins.
symptoms: Query performance degradation after increasing memory settings.
Sequential scans also showed slower performance.
mechanism: Memory allocation changes affected caching behavior, leading to slower query execution due to altered interaction between PostgreSQL shared buffers and OS-level caching.

facts.evidence: Post author observed slower query performance with increased work_mem settings.
Post author observed slower query performance with increased shared_buffers settings.

facts.key: Hash Join slower with increased buffers
facts.evidence: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) showed slower Hash Join operations.

facts.key: Sequential scans slower with increased buffers
facts.evidence: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) showed slower sequential scans.
Post author and commenters hypothesized interaction between PostgreSQL shared buffers and OS-level caching.

assumptions: PostgreSQL 9.2 behavior is representative of the issue.
Synthetic data can reproduce query plans and caching behavior.
Default_statistics_target and other settings remain unchanged.
unknowns: Exact impact of OS-level caching on query performance.
Whether the issue persists in newer PostgreSQL versions.
